title: Japan Plans to Make It Easier to Become a Teacher
paragraphs: Japan is planning to make it easier for working adults, or students who majored in another subject, to switch to a career in teaching.

A government education panel released a proposal on November 17 to make teaching licenses easier to get. The goal is to encourage more people to enter a profession that is struggling to find enough staff.

One change would make it easier for university students to qualify. At the moment, those preparing to teach in elementary, junior high or high schools must earn 59 credits in teaching-related subjects. Under the new plan, this would fall to 36 or 37 credits.

Students would still need another 20 credits, but these could come from subjects they are already studying for their degree. This would make it easier for students from different fields to become teachers.

The proposal would also include a one-year graduate course for working adults who hold a university degree or higher. They would learn about teaching and spend time working in schools, where they would also receive compensation.
The plan comes as schools across Japan struggle to find enough workers.
According to an education ministry survey, more than 2,800 public schools in Japan started the 2025 academic year without enough teachers.
And fewer people are choosing teaching jobs. In 2025, there were just 2.9 people applying for every teaching job, down from 3.2 a year earlier. That was the lowest number on record.
The panel plans to finalize its recommendations by the end of 2026, with changes to the law expected to be proposed in 2027.
